text:
lena: heads-up, onboarding for tenant 'beta-corp' failing this morning. SCIM calls intermittently 401 from IdP and our audit shows token.verify errors with "no matching kid" around 2026-03-20T08:22Z. anyone seen this pattern?

mike: short: kid mismatch usually means JWKs rotated and our jwks cache is stale, or client secret rotation created tokens signed by a different key. can you paste the introspect log?

lena: log excerpt:
```
2026-03-20T08:21:59Z INFO provisioner: request oauth2/introspect for client=beta-provisioner
2026-03-20T08:22:00Z ERROR oauth: introspect failed: HTTP 401 {"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"JWT signature verification failed: no matching kid"}
2026-03-20T08:22:00Z WARN provisioner: scim create aborted due to invalid token
```

anika: two related operations happened yesterday: customer rotated the client_secret and IdP applied a hotfix that rotated JWKs. if the token was minted with the old private key but the IdP removed the old kid from jwks, introspect will fail with that error.

mike: also check if the token was minted using client_credentials by our service with the old secret. run `curl https://idp.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json` and compare kids, and run `curl -X POST https://idp.example.com/oauth2/introspect -d 'token=<token>' -u client:secret` from the provisioning host (sts identity).

lena: fetched jwks; response only contains kid "k2" now, our logs show token header had kid "k1". so the IdP removed k1. but why did we receive a token with k1 after rotation?

anika: possible race where a worker minted a token before the client's secret rotation but used cached token later, or there are multiple token issuers (legacy instance) still minting with old key. also some IdP vendors have a setting to keep both keys for a window; if they removed k1 early due to CVE mitigation we may see this.

mike: good point. also check CloudTrail-like audit on customer IdP for token issuance timestamps and which client used which key.

security-bot: vulnerability note: CVE-2026-0147 reported in idp-issuer 4.x where hotfix may rotate keys immediately for safety; vendor advisory recommends coordinate rotation with relying parties. confirm vendor and version.

lena: reached out to customer. they confirm they applied a security hotpatch last night and rotated jwks to mitigate CVE-2026-0147; they also rotated client secrets in a separate change. they've pinned the old secret for a short TTL but removed k1 from jwks earlier than expected.

mike: remediation plan I propose:
- Invalidate jwks cache on all provisioning pods when we detect 401 with "no matching kid" (add automatic refresh path).
- Log token.kid in audit events for better triage.
- Add a short-lived compatibility flow: on introspect 401 + kid mismatch, attempt token re-fetch using current client_secret and retry once.
- Add a cross-team runbook: coordinate IdP key rotations and secret rotation windows with customers.

anika: also found missing user.link audit rows: when introspect failed we aborted before emitting user.link; we should replay any successful SCIM creates from DLQ that lack audit rows. I can run a targeted replay for beta-corp for 08:15-08:30.

lena: please do. also please add a health check that asserts jwks freshness and alerts if jwks age > 5m for active tenants.

idsrv-bot: performed jwks cache refresh on provisioning-prod pool (job jwks-refresh-20260320-01).

mike: I'll open an RFC to add the retry-on-kid-mismatch path and the audit token.kid field. I'll also coordinate with solutions to ask customers to schedule rotations.

lena: DLQ replay started for beta-corp window 08:15-08:30. will report results.

anika: DLQ replay complete, re-emitted missing user.link events; audit index reconciled. provisioning attempts succeeded after jwks refresh.

lena: postmortem notes: root cause = IdP hotpatch removed old JWK (k1) during secret/key rotations; secondary = our jwks cache and lack of token.kid in audit. remediations implemented: jwks refresh path, audit token.kid, DLQ replay, runbook for coordinated rotations. closing when RFC merged. thanks all :thumbsup:
